comms_raw:
RF Modem, Iridium (RUDICS), integrated ARGOS, optional Acoustic
Modem
sensors_raw: Over 50 sensor options, incl.: ADCP; acoustic modem; optical transmission; passive acoustic monitoring / hydrophones; beam attenuation; CTD (pumped or unpumped); echosounder; fish-tag detection; nitrate; optical backscatter, attenuation and fluorometry; oxygen; PAR; radiometer; particle size; particle/biology imaging; turbidity; turbulence; custom integrations (wet payload / backseat driver capable)

comms_raw: Uses the Slocum communications architecture (Iridium; RF / ARGOS integrated)
sensors_raw: Up to 8 sensor/hardware integrations; same catalogue as Slocum (ADCP, acoustic modem, PAM/hydrophones, CTD, echosounder, fish-tag detection, nitrate, optics, oxygen, PAR, radiometer, turbidity, turbulence, custom) - pitched at high-power payloads (active/passive acoustics, onboard processing, imaging)

range_raw: 4,600 km (650 dives to 1 km) [Kongsberg]; up to 6,000 km [1KA guide]
depth_raw: 50 - 1000 m (practical shallow limit ~50-75 m; most efficient deep)
comms_raw: Iridium (RUDICS / dial-up); acoustic transponder; optional Argos tag, optional acoustic modem
sensors_raw: CTD (Sea-Bird CT sail, GPCTD); DO (Aanderaa optode, Sea-Bird); fluorescence/backscatter (WET Labs ECO puck, SeaOWL, Turner Cyclops); PAR; echosounder (Imagenex 853, 120 kHz); ADCP; passive acoustic monitoring; microstructure turbulence; pCO2 optode. 4 serial + 1 frequency sensor channels

deployment_length_raw: 12 months nominal (SGX doc); IOP reports year-plus Seaglider missions, longest 22 months under ice
depth_raw: Rated 1000 m; UW guidance: stay deeper than 200 m offshore and 75 m coastal
comms_raw: Iridium 9523 (RUDICS; PSTN dial-up for testing), optional acoustic modem
sensors_raw: Standard: RBR Legato CTD, optics, oxygen optode. Optional: microstructure, passive acoustics, irradiance (OCR-504), ADCP (Nortek Signature1000), WET Labs triplet; scicon science controller

Modular nose payloads (shared with SE1000): RBR Legato/CODA ODO/Tridente, Sea-Bird GPCTD/SBE43F/SUNA/UBAT, JFE Rinko AROD, Nortek AD2CP, WET Labs ECO (FLBBCD, FLNTU...), SeaOWL, Biospherical PAR, Rockland MR1000G microstructure, UVP6, Imagenex echosounder, Franatech METS methane, Pro-Oceanus Mini-CO2, ANB pH, lab-on-chip, PAM (Alseamar AURIS 4-hydrophone, Turbulent Research Porpoise)
Same modular payload catalogue as SeaExplorer 200; up to 6 sensors in a wet + dry bay (max 9 L / 8 kg); end-user sensor API; altimeter fitted

range_raw: 4,700 km at 19 deg glide / 3,500 km at 25 deg (1000 m ops)
depth_raw: Max 1500 m; typical operations to 1000 m
comms_raw: Iridium (two-way, ~100 bytes/s); combined GPS/Iridium antennas in each wing (glider rolls 90 deg at surface)
sensors_raw: CTD (PME; Sea-Bird 41CP pumped); Seapoint optical backscatter and chlorophyll fluorometer; Tritech altimeter; Sontek Argonaut 750 kHz ADCP

deployment_length_raw: 100+ days; 500+ profiles to 1000 m per mission
sensors_raw: Standard: Sea-Bird GPCTD. Supported: Seapoint chlorophyll fluorometer, SBE-63 DO, Nortek AD2CP. Connections for 8 RS-232 sensors, up to 1 Hz

depth_raw: 200 m operational; can work in very shallow water (<6 m)
comms_raw: Iridium SBD; Wi-Fi 802.11abg (high-gain antenna); Ethernet; LED strobe
sensors_raw: Standard: JFE CT (ACTD-OEMU-Z105), Keller PA-7LH pressure, Nortek altimeter. OceanScout-PAM: HTI-92-WB hydrophone, 2 Hz-50 kHz, 2 TB storage, up to 250 kSPS, 24-bit; underway or hover modes

depth_raw: Up to 1500 m (dived 1,514.2 m in trials)
10,000 m class: 8,213 m (Apr 2018); 10,619 m world record (Mariana Trench, Jul 2020)

comms_raw: Iridium (SBD and RUDICS); RF (900 MHz, 460 MHz, others); Wi-Fi 802.11n
sensors_raw: 6 sensor mounting points / 5 external connectors (1 fwd, 4 aft); AML X-Change / Smart-X field-swappable sensor heads (up to 11 at once); acoustic altimeter standard; watertight electronics bay 8.6 L for user electronics or a third-party science computer; nominal payload 5 kg
Passive acoustic sensing processed on board by Lura, Helsing's 'large acoustic model' (detect, classify, localise vessels and submarines)
